scenes.title: Radar sends waves and receives echoes
The antenna launches a radio pulse
Repeated scans build an echo map

vo.text: A radar finds distant objects by sending out radio waves and listening for their echoes.
vo.speak: A radar finds distant objects by sending out radio waves and listening for their echoes.

vo.text: This works in darkness because radio echoes do not need visible light.
vo.speak: This works in darkness because radio echoes do not need visible light.

vo.text: The radar's transmitter creates a short radio pulse, and its antenna sends that pulse into space.
vo.speak: The radar's transmitter creates a short radio pulse, and its antenna sends that pulse into space.

vo.text: The pulse travels outward at the speed of light until it reaches an object such as an aircraft.
vo.speak: The pulse travels outward at the speed of light until it reaches an object such as an aircraft.

vo.text: Some radio energy reflects from the aircraft and returns toward the radar antenna.
vo.speak: Some radio energy reflects from the aircraft and returns toward the radar antenna.

vo.text: The radar measures the echo's round-trip time to calculate distance.
vo.speak: The radar measures the echo's round-trip time to calculate distance.

vo.text: Multiplying half that time by the speed of light gives the object's range.
vo.speak: Multiplying half that time by the speed of light gives the object's range.

vo.text: A rotating antenna repeats this process in different directions, building a map of echoes around the radar.
vo.speak: A rotating antenna repeats this process in different directions, building a map of echoes around the radar.

vo.text: So radar locates objects by timing radio-wave echoes rather than relying on visible light.
vo.speak: So radar locates objects by timing radio-wave echoes rather than relying on visible light.
